analysis.title: Liquid Insight: Global rates and oil: Close cousins
key_insights: BofA finds strong evidence that higher oil prices lead to higher inflation compensation in US, UK and German interest rates. The relationship holds across decades of data.
Real rates generally fall when oil rises, but the US bucked this in 2026. The ratio of up-to-down moves for US real rates was about 3 to 1 this year versus a historical norm near 0.9 to 1.

BofA attributes the 2026 US real-rate anomaly to the capex boom lifting real rates when oil is not rising. Over the last month the ratio has moved back toward 0.9 to 1, which BofA reads as the capex boom being largely priced.
YTD 2026, US 2y swap rates rose 113bp in total, but rose 196bp on oil-up days and fell 83bp on other days. UK 2y rose 109bp (375bp up, -266bp down) and German 2y rose 91bp (313bp up, -222bp down).
UK 2y inflation compensation rose 511bp on oil-up days YTD and fell 393bp on other days. German 2y inflation compensation showed the same pattern (+488bp / -393bp).

Since 12/31/2008 (4,460 days), US 2y inflation swaps rose a cumulative 3802bp on oil-up days and fell 3375bp on other days. Real rates fell 2509bp on oil-up days and rose 2441bp on other days. Breakevens drove the nominal moves.

BofA expects rates to rise substantially if oil keeps rising over the next 3-6 months, especially at the front end where monetary policy expectations matter more than term premium. The chain is higher energy prices, higher inflation compensation, higher hike expectations at central banks, then more hikes.

BofA thinks the Fed would be less constrained than other central banks if energy inflation rises, citing resilient US growth and consumption, inflation above target since the pandemic and tight labor markets.

Oil likely already carries a significant risk premium, and further gains are not guaranteed. The near-term path depends on the duration and intensity of the Ukraine and Middle East conflicts. Markets priced a higher chance of resolving the Iran conflict after the US elections.

Crude buffers have fallen. The EIA estimates a roughly 500mn barrel decline YTD against a rough working estimate of 1.5bn barrels of global buffer capacity. Brookings argues price increases could accelerate if buffers fall far enough.

Refinery capacity is reduced by both conflicts. Diesel rose 76% this year from an average of $3.5/gallon to $6.25. The IEA estimates Ukraine cut Russian refinery throughput by about 30%, or about 2% of global throughput. Energy analysts estimate Iran cut Gulf refinery throughput by around 2% of global supply.
BofA sees asymmetric risk for the Fed. It can stay on hold in the most dovish scenario but may have to seek an unknown restrictive level in the most hawkish one.

BofA recommends considering hedges: shorter-term inflation protection in the US, UK and Germany, and a pay-fixed position in US 2y rates. It argues the Fed will not be able to push back on market hike pricing going into meetings.
BofA warns that a new Fed Chair without established inflation credibility who holds rates in meetings with over 50% chance of a hike priced could lose control of long-end rates.

trade_ideas.description: Hold shorter-term inflation protection in US, UK and Germany
trade_ideas.rationale: Higher oil reliably lifts inflation compensation, and extended conflict could push oil higher.
BofA thinks the Fed will not be able to push back on market pricing of hikes going into meetings.
trade_ideas.risk: A resolution of the Iran conflict and a drop in oil would lower inflation compensation and rates.

risk_factors: Extended conflict in Iran and Ukraine could push oil and rates sharply higher.
Falling crude buffers could accelerate oil price increases.
Reduced refinery capacity from attacks in both conflicts keeps product prices elevated.
A new Fed Chair with unestablished inflation credibility may lose control of long-end rates if the Fed holds in meetings with over 50% hike probability priced.
Oil may already carry a significant risk premium, so a resolution could reverse the rate move.
charts_described: Chart of the day: 2026 YTD table splitting days into oil-up and other days, showing US 2y swaps +113bp (+196bp up days, -83bp other days) with inflation and real rate components.
Exhibit 1: 2y inflation swaps in US, UK and EU plotted against CO1 crude since 2016, with the UK 2y inflation swap especially responsive in 2026.
Exhibit 2: 12/31/2008-11/4/2026 changes in nominal swaps, inflation and real rates on oil-up and other days for US, UK and Germany.
geopolitical: Iran conflict: restricted crude flows out of Gulf producers, and Iran has targeted Gulf refineries. Markets priced a higher chance of resolution after the US elections.
Ukraine-Russia war: Ukraine has attacked Russian refineries, cutting throughput by about 30% per the IEA, and Ukraine leadership said in October it intends to continue.
BofA notes that even if the Iran conflict settles, Gulf supply may not return reliably to its pre-war rate.

tension_points.bull_case: Oil may already carry a significant risk premium. Markets priced a higher chance of resolving the Iran conflict after the US elections, which would let the Fed stay on hold.
tension_points.bear_case: Extended conflict in Iran and Ukraine, falling crude buffers and reduced refinery capacity could push oil and rates substantially higher. The Fed may need to enter restrictive territory.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Resolution or a marked settling of the Iran conflict, or oil failing to rise over the next 3-6 months, would undercut the higher-rates call.

theme_stances.evidence: if oil prices continue to rise over the next 3-6 months

theme_stances.key_argument: The US capex boom lifted real rates when oil was not rising, and the effect may now be priced in.
theme_stances.evidence: the capex boom might now be well baked into the price
